1 قَمِرَ , aor.
قَمَرَ , (S, A, K,) inf. n. قَمَرٌ, (S,) He, (a man, S, A, K, and an antelope, and a bird, TA,) and it, (a man's sight, A,) became dazzled (S, A, K) in the moonlight, (A,) or by snow, (S, A, K,) so that he could not see: (S, A:) he (an antelope) became deprived of his sight by the light of the moon, so that he was perplexed, and unable to see his right course. (IKtt.) ―
-b2- قَمِرَ, aor.
قَمَرَ , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He (a man, TA,) was, or became, sleepless in the moonlight. (K.) ＝
-A2- See also 3, throughout.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
